## Summary

Lets **offline packed data feed global-batch packing and dynamic context parallelism (DCP)**. Until now the two were mutually exclusive, so DCP (#6682) only ran on online, unpacked samples. With both `enable_offline_packing` and `enable_global_batch_packing` set, each offline packed row yields one unpacked sample per sequence it holds. Megatron-Core's scheduler then re-bins those sequences and, under DCP, picks a CP group for each bin. The global batch counts packed rows, as in the original Megatron-LM agentic SFT example's `offline_dynamic_cp` mode.

**Stacked on #6682** (mock dataset, recipe): review the commits from `feat(data): feed offline packed rows…` on. Draft until #6682 and NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7048 land.

## Megatron-Core pin: NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7048 (temporary, do not merge as is)

As in #6682, `3rdparty/Megatron-LM` / `.main.commit` point to the head of **NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7048** ("[DCP V2 4/4] Propagate runtime dynamic CP through hybrid model layers"). Without it, a dynamic-CP bin on a group smaller than the base CP fails in Qwen3.5's Gated DeltaNet layers.

- This branch pins **`f1aa086`**, #7048's current head. It is main's pin `e0a4bfed` plus #7048 (35 ahead, 0 behind), with an unchanged MCore `pyproject.toml`, so `uv.lock` matches main.
- The earlier #7048 head `e3165e9`, which #6682 still pins, lacks MCore changes that Bridge main now needs (for example `OptimizerConfig.validate`).
- Re-pin to main's commit once #7048 merges.

**Result (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, one 4×GB200 node, NeMo 26.10, mock mixed-length data, 200 steps):**

| Packing | Static CP4 tokens/s | Dynamic CP tokens/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Online, 32 samples/step | 12,157 | 13,301 |
| Offline, eight 64K rows/step | **14,450** | 12,463 |

Offline packing with DCP works end to end on both mock and real data. But on offline rows, **static CP4 is the fastest setup (+18.9% over online static, +8.6% over online DCP), and DCP is 13.8% slower than static on identical rows**. Details under [Validation](#validation).

## Changes

| Area | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Packed GPT-SFT data | `GPTSFTPackedDataset` (`.npy` and, by inheritance, Parquet) gets a global-batch collate that splits each row into one scheduler sample per sequence. Each sample keeps its in-sequence next-token labels and the row's loss mask. Alignment padding written by offline packing (zero-loss EOS tails) is stripped and replaced by the global-batch alignment multiple, `2 x dp x cp` under DCP, so rows prepared with any `pad_seq_to_mult` work. |
| Builder | Passes `enable_global_batch_packing`, the alignment multiple and `fold_alignment_padding` to the packed dataset classes. |
| Validation | `GPTSFTDatasetConfig` and `ConfigContainer` accept offline + global-batch packing; global-batch stays exclusive with in-batch and Energon packing. `pad_cu_seqlens` (a CUDA-graph feature) is rejected with global-batch packing. The bin-capacity check also covers `packed_sequence_size`. |
| Mock data | `MockGPTSFTDatasetConfig.enable_offline_packing` + `offline_packing_specs`: the mock samples are packed first-fit decreasing into rows (aligned lengths, deterministic, rows shuffled with the seed). Each item is one row and yields its samples. |
| Recipe | `qwen35_text_35b_a3b_4gpu_gb200_fp8mx_offline_dynamic_cp_config`: the #6682 recipe with 64K offline rows and a global batch of 8 rows. Add `model.dynamic_context_parallel=false` for static CP4 on the same rows. |
| Example tool | `compare_runs.py` takes per-run global batch / packed row size and compares by runtime tokens per second, so runs that process different work per step can be compared. |
| Docs | `packed-sequences.md` and `dynamic-context-parallel.md` (+ Fern mirrors): new "Offline Packed Rows" sections and the measurements; `examples/agentic_sft/README.md`: commands and results. |

## Validation

All performance runs: `nvcr.io/nvidia/nemo:26.10`, MCore `e3165e9` (the #7048 head at the time, as in #6682), on this branch before its latest merge of main. On the current head (main merged, MCore `f1aa086`), the unit tests and a 30-step smoke run of the offline DCP recipe were repeated: the same 579 passed / 1 skipped / 1 failed (the DeepEP-on-GB200 test below), and 30 steps with no skipped iterations, finite losses (12.83 to 12.82), grad norms 68-70, and steady 39-54 s steps.

### Mock data, 4-GPU recipe

Full 40-layer Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + MTP1, TP1/PP1/base CP4/EP4, MXFP8, CPU optimizer offload, HybridEP, full recompute. 200 steps, steps 1-10 excluded; tokens/s from `compare_runs.py`:

| Packing | Mode | Mean s/step | Runtime tokens/s | Median model TFLOP/s per GPU |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Online, GBS 32 samples | Static CP4 | 55.98 | 12,157 | 96 |
| Online, GBS 32 samples | Dynamic CP | 51.16 | 13,301 | 106 |
| Offline, GBS 8 rows | Static CP4 | 36.27 | 14,450 | 113 |
| Offline, GBS 8 rows | Dynamic CP | 42.05 | 12,463 | 101 |

**Correctness:**
- Offline DCP and offline static start from the same rows: step 1 LM loss 12.83670 vs 12.83668, grad norm 70.11 vs 70.08.
- Losses and gradients stay finite with no skipped steps.
- The online DCP run on this branch reproduces #6682's online run: identical step-1/2 losses, 13,301 vs 13,069 tokens/s.

**Why offline DCP is slower than offline static:**
- First-fit decreasing fills rows to a mean 100.0% of 64K, so each step carries a nearly constant 524K tokens (stdev 1.2K, against 682K ± 93K online).
- Static CP4 (order-preserving `dp_balanced`) keeps those rows as 8 full CP4 bins.
- DCP re-bins the same sequences into 9.05 microbatches per step, against 8.00 for static, at the same per-rank critical path (both simulated with Megatron-Core's own schedulers on the run's lengths). Online it is the reverse, 11.3 against 13.7, which is where DCP gains.
- Measured on identical rows, DCP is −13.8% (95% bootstrap −16.5% to −10.9%; wins 8 of 190 paired steps).
- After its longer warmup (each new group size compiles on first use; about 40 steps), DCP is −9.7% over steps 41-200, close to the microbatch ratio.
- The original example reported offline DCP 14,925 vs online DCP 14,342 tokens/s on its own data, but did not measure offline static.

### Real data, 8-GPU CoderForge recipe (GPT-SFT offline packed Parquet)

`qwen35_text_35b_a3b_sft_8gpu_gb200_bf16_dynamic_cp_config` with `dataset.enable_offline_packing=true`:
- the first 4,000 SWE-Rebench trajectories, packed into 32K rows (`pad_seq_to_mult` 8) by the GPT-SFT builder
- random init, global batch 64 rows, 2×4 GB200 in one NVL72 rack, 12 steps, steps 5-12 reported

This exercises the new `GPTSFTPackedDataset` collate with DP2 × CP4:

| Configuration | Median step | Median TFLOP/s per GPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Online DCP (#6682 table, 64 trajectories/step) | 79 s | 100 |
| Online static CP4 (#6682 table) | 75 s | 106 |
| Offline DCP, 64 rows/step | 68 s | 116 |
| Offline static CP4, same rows | 61 s | 127 |

- Offline runs avoid the online loader stalls, because data is pre-tokenized: the online runs had 200-280 s steps while lazily tokenizing.
- About nine in ten trajectories exceed the 32K cap, so DCP has no short sequences to exploit, and static wins in both modes.

### Unit tests

New tests:
- the packed-row split, flattening and offline-padding replacement (`tests/unit_tests/data/packing/test_global_batch.py`)
- config validation (`test_config.py`: offline rows feeding DCP with the pool alignment; bin capacity; `pad_cu_seqlens`)
- mock offline rows (`test_mock_gpt_sft.py`)
- the offline recipe (`test_qwen35_dynamic_cp_mock_recipe.py`)

Run with the affected suites (`test_gpt_sft_config.py`, `test_gpt_sft.py`, `test_parquet.py`, `test_paths.py`, `test_packed_seq_utils.py`, the Qwen3.5 recipe tests) on a GB200 node: **579 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed**. The failure is `test_native_energon_packing_allows_other_ep_dispatchers_with_fixed_width[flex]`: DeepEP does not support GB200, and the test covers code this PR does not touch.

```bash
uv run python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/data/packing/test_global_batch.py \
    tests/unit_tests/data/builders/test_mock_gpt_sft.py \
    tests/unit_tests/recipes/qwen/test_qwen35_dynamic_cp_mock_recipe.py \
    tests/unit_tests/training/test_config.py -k "global_batch or offline or GlobalBatch"
```

## Notes

- Making DCP keep pre-packed full rows as CP4 bins would be a Megatron-Core scheduler change, not part of this PR.
- `train.global_batch_size` counts packed rows with offline packing, so equal GBS does not mean equal work. `compare_runs.py` compares such runs by tokens per second.

+  here, and the packing scheduler pulls a whole step's samples at once. With
+  two loader workers the GPUs wait on data; the recipe uses 16.

+samples. Hybrid models such as Qwen3.5 need
+[Megatron-LM #7048](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7048) for bins
+that run on a group smaller than the base CP.

+Train from scratch with dynamic CP, then add
+`model.dynamic_context_parallel=false` for the static-CP4 baseline:
+
+```bash
+uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=4 scripts/training/run_recipe.py \
+  --recipe qwen35_text_35b_a3b_4gpu_gb200_fp8mx_dynamic_cp_config --mode pretrain \
+  train.train_iters=200 scheduler.lr_decay_iters=200 scheduler.lr_warmup_iters=20
+```

+# Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with dynamic context parallelism on 4×GB200
+
+`qwen35_text_35b_a3b_4gpu_gb200_fp8mx_dynamic_cp_config` trains the **full 40-layer Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (plus one MTP
+layer)** on one four-GPU GB200 node with **dynamic** context parallelism (CP), on **mock data** whose sample lengths
+follow an agentic tool-use workload. Dynamic CP runs each packed bin on a CP1, CP2 or CP4 group sized for its longest
+sequence instead of splitting every bin across the full CP4 group. This directory shows how to run the recipe in both
+modes and compare them.
+
+The model and training configuration follow the Megatron-LM agentic SFT example by Zhongbo Zhu
+([`examples/agentic_sft`, commit `420686e`](https://github.com/zhongbozhu/Megatron-LM/commit/420686e1a7e9d51d422e8ac1a18a35818843bb86)):
+TP1/PP1/base CP4/EP4/ETP1, 64K context, micro batch 1, global batch 32, per-token loss, MXFP8 compute, FP32 Adam state
+offloaded to the host, HybridEP and full recompute. The model is built from the pinned Hugging Face config through the
+Qwen3.5 bridge.
+
+## Requirements
+
+* Four GB200 GPUs and a container with Transformer Engine, CuTeDSL and DeepEP HybridEP.
+* Megatron-Core with [NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#7048](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7048), which propagates
+  the runtime CP group through the Gated DeltaNet layers. Without it, a bin on a group smaller than the base CP fails
+  with `GDN: cu_seqlens_q[-1]=16384 does not match total_sequence_length=65536`.
+* A large host-memory allocation for the CPU optimizer.
+
+## Mock data
+
+`MockGPTSFTDatasetConfig` generates random token IDs, so no dataset or tokenizer is read. Half of the samples need at
+most CP1 capacity (up to 16K tokens), 30% need CP2 (16K–32K) and 20% need CP4 (32K–64K), with lengths uniform inside
+each bucket. That puts about 19% / 35% / 46% of the tokens in the three buckets and averages 21K tokens per sample,
+close to the original example's mixed data (19% / 36% / 45%). The last 20% of each sample is supervised. Lengths and
+tokens are deterministic in the seed, so two runs see identical samples in identical order. The loss is not
+meaningful: random tokens have nothing to learn.
+
+## Run
+
+From scratch, as in the original example:
+
+```bash
+uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=4 scripts/training/run_recipe.py \
+    --recipe qwen35_text_35b_a3b_4gpu_gb200_fp8mx_dynamic_cp_config --mode pretrain \
+    train.train_iters=200 scheduler.lr_decay_iters=200 scheduler.lr_warmup_iters=20
+```
+
+Static-CP4 baseline on the same packing path and the same data:
+
+```bash
+uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=4 scripts/training/run_recipe.py \
+    --recipe qwen35_text_35b_a3b_4gpu_gb200_fp8mx_dynamic_cp_config --mode pretrain \
+    train.train_iters=200 scheduler.lr_decay_iters=200 scheduler.lr_warmup_iters=20 \
+    model.dynamic_context_parallel=false
+```
+
+Offline packing, as the original example's `offline_dynamic_cp` mode: the same samples are packed ahead of time,
+first-fit decreasing, into 64K-token rows, each step takes eight rows, and dynamic CP re-bins their samples. Add
+`model.dynamic_context_parallel=false` for static CP4 on the same rows:
+
+```bash
+uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=4 scripts/training/run_recipe.py \
+    --recipe qwen35_text_35b_a3b_4gpu_gb200_fp8mx_offline_dynamic_cp_config --mode pretrain \
+    train.train_iters=200 scheduler.lr_decay_iters=200 scheduler.lr_warmup_iters=20
+```
+
+To start from converted weights, use `--mode sft` with `checkpoint.pretrained_checkpoint=/path/to/megatron/checkpoint`.
+Nothing is saved unless `checkpoint.save` is set; a full-model checkpoint with optimizer state is about 460 GB.

+memory on these variable-length batches, and NCCL then fails to create the communicator it builds lazily at the end of

+## Compare the two runs
+
+Keep each run's log. The first steps include one-time compilation, so they are excluded. With the mock dataset's
+settings, `compare_runs.py` also reports runtime tokens per second and compares by it:
+
+```bash
+uv run python examples/agentic_sft/compare_runs.py --baseline static.log --candidate dynamic.log --warmup 10 \
+    --mock-seq-length 65536 --train-iters 200 --global-batch-size 32

+

+"""Compare the steady-state throughput of two training logs, for example static versus dynamic context parallelism.
+
+The script reads Bridge's per-iteration log lines, drops the warmup iterations (which include one-time compilation),
+and reports seconds per step. For runs of the ``qwen35_text_35b_a3b_4gpu_gb200_fp8mx_*dynamic_cp_config`` recipes it
+also reports runtime tokens per second: the ``MockGPTSFTDatasetConfig`` lengths are deterministic, and samples (or,
+with offline packing, packed rows) are consumed in order, so iteration ``i`` processes items
+``(i - 1) * global_batch_size`` to ``i * global_batch_size - 1``. The gain is then the ratio of tokens per second, so
+runs that process different work per step, such as online and offline packing, can be compared. Without token counts,
+both runs must have consumed the same data in the same order and the gain is the ratio of step times.
+
+Example::
+
+    python examples/agentic_sft/compare_runs.py --baseline online.log --candidate offline.log --warmup 10 \\
+        --mock-seq-length 65536 --train-iters 200 --baseline-global-batch-size 32 \\
+        --candidate-global-batch-size 8 --candidate-packed-sequence-size 65536
+"""

+
+import argparse
+import logging
+import re
+import statistics
+from pathlib import Path
+

+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_ITERATION = re.compile(
+    r"iteration\s+(?P<iteration>\d+)/\s*\d+\s*\|\s*consumed samples:\s*(?P<samples>\d+)\s*\|\s*"
+    r"elapsed time per iteration \(ms\):\s*(?P<ms>[0-9.]+)"
+)
+_LM_LOSS = re.compile(r"lm loss:\s*(?P<loss>[0-9.]+E[+-]\d+)")
+
+
+def parse_log(text: str) -> dict[int, dict[str, float]]:
+    """Return ``{iteration: {"seconds": ..., "loss": ...}}`` from Bridge training log text.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If the log has no iteration lines.
+    """
+    steps: dict[int, dict[str, float]] = {}
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        match = _ITERATION.search(line)
+        if match is None:
+            continue
+        step = {"seconds": float(match["ms"]) / 1000.0}
+        loss = _LM_LOSS.search(line)
+        if loss is not None:
+            step["loss"] = float(loss["loss"])
+        steps[int(match["iteration"])] = step
+    if not steps:
+        raise ValueError("No iteration lines found; is this a Bridge training log?")
+    return steps
+

+    """Runtime tokens consumed by each iteration, with rows taken in file order."""
+    return {
+        iteration: sum(lengths[(iteration - 1) * global_batch_size : iteration * global_batch_size])
+        for iteration in iterations
+    }
